The reason I filed this issue is because my renderer was very stable in 1.x, but in 2.0 it degrades very quickly, which suggests to me some kind of resource leak in Zone.  I notice a large amount of time being spent on what appears to be patching get/set properties.

issue.title: bug: `requestAnimationFrame` zone grows forever

body:
I dug into this a little bit, and it appears that the requestAnimationFrame wrapper in zone.js is flawed.

I filed an issue over there: https://github.com/angular/zone.js/issues/143

issue.title: fix(patch): do not leak zones when wrapping requestAnimationFrame
issue.body:
# Problem

requestAnimationFrame is often called from within the callback function that is bound to its zone.  This results in every subsequent call to the same function creating and binding to a new zone.
# Proposed Solution

Maintain a simple reference count of function signatures given to requestAnimationFrame, and when the reference count is greater than 0 bind to to the parent zone rather than creating a new one.

Feedback welcome.

Fixes: #143, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/2912
